goal.value: Pilot an in-country WhatsApp AI agent for Shifa Clinics that reads Arabic/English patient messages, assesses urgency, books the right appointment directly in the clinic calendar (book/cancel only), and instantly alerts a nurse for emergencies and nurse-callback cases. Pilot covers Riyadh Olaya and Jeddah Rawdah.
goal.source: Client brief.pdf; Kickoff transcript.txt; Scope email.eml

success_metric.value: During the 4-week pilot: (1) 100% of emergencies in the nurse-approved test set and live pilot get emergency advice (call 997/ED) plus a nurse alert within 30 seconds, and none are offered a routine appointment (zero missed emergencies); (2) at least 95% of messages get a reply within 2 minutes, 24/7; (3) every message involving a child under 2 is routed to a nurse; (4) appointment-type and urgency routing agree with reception-staff labels on a held-out set at a target of 90% or higher (target to be confirmed).

value: 1. Patient safety: never miss an emergency; chest pain etc. is never offered a routine appointment; emergency advice plus nurse alert within 30 s
2. Nurse-owned escalation rules: use the head nurse-approved emergency symptom list, and always escalate children under 2 to a nurse; the agent does not decide emergencies alone
3. Data compliance: all patient data and models stay in-country/in-region
4. Reply within 2 minutes, day and night, in Arabic and English
5. Correct direct booking in the clinic calendar (find_slots/book/cancel only, no deletes, 10 req/s limit)
6. Deliver the pilot in 4 weeks at 2 clinics
priorities.source: Client brief.pdf; Kickoff transcript.txt; Scope email.eml

gaps.question: Which symptoms are always emergencies? The head nurse has not signed off a final list and does not want the agent deciding alone. Who approves the list, and by when?
gaps.suggested: Start from the triage guidelines' always-emergency list: chest pain or pressure, difficulty breathing, stroke signs, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness and seizure. Reply with a call-997 or go-to-the-ED message and send a nurse alert. The head nurse signs off the final list, including Arabic phrasings, before week 2. Anything ambiguous goes to a nurse.

gaps.question: Who receives nurse alerts at night and on weekends, and what happens if no nurse acknowledges an alert? The 24/7 two-minute reply and the 30-second alert depend on this.
gaps.suggested: Confirm that the nurse station app is staffed or has an on-call nurse 24/7 at both pilot clinics. If an alert is not acknowledged within 5 minutes, escalate to a backup nurse or the head nurse. The agent always gives the patient emergency advice immediately and does not wait for the nurse.

gaps.question: No success metric or acceptance threshold was given. What counts as pilot success, for example the share of messages answered within 2 minutes and the booking accuracy needed?
gaps.suggested: Zero missed emergencies on the nurse-approved test set and in live pilot review. At least 95% of replies within 2 minutes. At least 90% routing agreement with reception labels. The operations manager and head nurse confirm these before build.

goal.value: Build a bilingual (Arabic/English) AI agent on WhatsApp that reads patient messages, classifies urgency, books the right appointment directly in the clinic calendar for routine and same-day needs, and immediately alerts a nurse for emergencies and nurse-callback cases. Pilot in 2 clinics (Riyadh Olaya, Jeddah Rawdah) for 4 weeks, ahead of rollout to all 8 Shifa clinics.
goal.source: Client brief.pdf; Scope email.eml; Kickoff transcript.txt

success_metric.value: Pilot targets: (1) 100% of emergency messages get emergency advice (call 997 or go to the ED) plus a nurse alert, and none is offered a routine appointment. (2) At least 95% of patient messages get a first reply within 2 minutes, 24/7. (3) Nurse alerts arrive within 30 seconds. (4) Booking accuracy and the share of messages handled without staff are tracked against the baseline of hours-long waits. Thresholds other than the 2-minute reply and the zero-missed-emergency rule are proposed, not client-stated.

value: 1. Patient safety: never miss an emergency. Rule-based safety checks sit on top of the ML urgency classifier. When uncertain, escalate.
2. Always route to a nurse: nurse-callback cases, including children under 2 and pregnancy with bleeding, and any symptom the head nurse has not cleared.
3. Reply within 2 minutes, day and night.
4. Book the correct appointment directly in the calendar for routine and same-day requests. Handle messages that mix symptoms and booking requests.
5. Support Arabic (about 82% of traffic) and English.
6. Deliver the 2-clinic pilot in 4 weeks.
Patient data must stay inside the country. Hosting is on the client's in-country cloud, and any models used must run in-region.
The calendar API allows booking and cancelling only. The agent must never delete records.
The head nurse must agree which symptoms are always emergencies. The agent must not decide this alone.
Children under 2 are always routed to a nurse.
Nurse alerts go to the nurse station app and include the patient's message and the agent's reason. They must arrive within 30 seconds.
Pilot scope is 2 clinics (Riyadh Olaya, Jeddah Rawdah), with Arabic and English only.
Emergency examples are rare (about 120 in 12,000 messages), so rule-based safety checks are needed.
constraints.source: Kickoff transcript.txt; Scope email.eml; integration-contract.md; message-data-notes.md

deadline.value: Pilot go-live in 4 weeks, in 2 clinics. The pilot itself runs for 4 weeks. The documents are ambiguous on whether the 4 weeks is time to launch or the pilot's length.

value: Operations manager (owner of the 2-minute reply and calendar booking requirements)
Head nurse (clinical sign-off on emergency criteria; receives nurse alerts)
IT manager (data residency, calendar API)
Patients (WhatsApp, Arabic and English)
Reception staff (tagged the historical data)
Clinic leadership at Shifa Clinics (8 clinics)

gaps.question: Who receives nurse alerts at night and on weekends? The agent replies 24/7, but the documents don't say whether the nurse station app is staffed around the clock, or what happens if an alert isn't acknowledged.
gaps.suggested: Confirm 24/7 nurse coverage for the 2 pilot clinics, or a named on-call nurse. If an alert isn't acknowledged within about 5 minutes, escalate to a second nurse. Meanwhile the agent keeps giving the patient emergency advice (call 997).

gaps.question: What are the pilot's pass/fail thresholds, and what does the agent do when it can't book? The brief gives no measurable acceptance criteria beyond the 2-minute reply and zero missed emergencies. It doesn't say whether the agent can reschedule or cancel appointments, or how it handles unclear messages.
gaps.suggested: Adopt these targets: 100% emergency recall, 95% of replies within 2 minutes, and at least 90% booking accuracy in a nurse-reviewed audit. Allow booking and cancelling, since the API supports both. If the agent can't resolve a message, hand it to reception.

goal.value: Build a bilingual (Arabic/English) AI agent for Shifa Clinics' WhatsApp channel that reads patient messages, classifies urgency, books the right appointment directly in the clinic calendar for routine and same-day cases, and immediately alerts a nurse for emergencies and nurse-callback cases. Pilot at 2 clinics (Riyadh Olaya, Jeddah Rawdah); the full network is 8 clinics, about 3,000 messages a week.
goal.source: Client brief.pdf; Scope email.eml; Kickoff transcript.txt

success_metric.value: Pilot targets. (1) Emergency recall: 100% of emergency messages in the clinically signed-off test set get emergency advice (call 997 / go to ED) plus a nurse alert, and none are offered an appointment. (2) 95% of patient messages get a first reply within 2 minutes, 24/7. (3) Nurse alerts arrive within 30 seconds. (4) Children under 2 with symptoms always go to a nurse. (5) Share of messages handled end to end without staff intervention is tracked as a secondary measure.
success_metric.source: Client brief.pdf; integration-contract.md (30 s alert); thresholds inferred

value: 1. Patient safety: never miss an emergency. Rule-based safety checks run on top of the ML classifier, and emergencies are never offered a routine appointment.
2. Escalate to a nurse: emergencies, children under 2, and cases like pregnancy bleeding. The head nurse's signed-off symptom list decides what counts, not the agent alone.
3. Reply within 2 minutes, day and night, in Arabic and English, including mixed messages such as symptoms plus a booking request.
4. Book the correct appointment directly in the calendar, using only find_slots, book and cancel. Never delete. Log every booking action for audit.
5. Keep patient data in-country: in-region hosting and in-region models only.
6. Deliver the 2-clinic pilot within 4 weeks.
Patient data must not leave the country. Hosting is the client's in-country cloud, and models must run in-region.
Calendar API supports find_slots, book and cancel only. No delete. Rate limit is 10 requests per second.
Approved stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI and the clinic calendar SDK. Every booking action is logged for audit.
Nurse alert goes to the nurse station app with the patient message and the agent's reason, within 30 seconds.
Languages: Arabic and English. Training data is about 82% Arabic. Only about 120 emergency examples exist, so safety rules are required on top of the classifier.
Emergency symptoms (chest pain, breathing difficulty, stroke signs, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, seizure) get a 997 / ED message plus a nurse alert.
Scope: pilot at Riyadh Olaya and Jeddah Rawdah only.
constraints.source: Kickoff transcript.txt; Scope email.eml; integration-contract.md; triage-guidelines.md

deadline.value: Pilot go-live in 4 weeks from kickoff, at 2 clinics (Riyadh Olaya, Jeddah Rawdah), running for 4 weeks.

value: Operations manager (owner of the 2-minute reply and direct booking requirements)
Head nurse (clinical sign-off on emergency symptoms and escalation rules; receives alerts)
IT manager (data residency, calendar API, hosting)
Nurses at the pilot clinics (alert recipients)
Reception staff (handle admin questions and fallback cases, and labelled the training data)
Patients (WhatsApp users, Arabic and English)

gaps.question: The head nurse says the list of symptoms that are always emergencies is not yet agreed, and she doesn't want the agent deciding alone. Who signs off the final emergency and nurse-callback list, and by when? The agent's safety rules and test set depend on it.
gaps.suggested: Use the guideline list as the starting point: chest pain or pressure, difficulty breathing, stroke signs, severe bleeding, loss of consciousness, seizure. Add the nurse-callback rules: child under 2 with symptoms, and pregnancy with bleeding. The head nurse signs off in writing by the end of week 1. If the list is still unsigned, the agent sends anything ambiguous to a nurse.

gaps.question: What measurable pass/fail threshold decides whether the pilot succeeds? The documents give only the 2-minute reply and 'never miss an emergency'. They give no target for emergency recall, over-escalation or booking accuracy.
gaps.suggested: Emergency recall of 100% on the signed-off test set and no emergency offered an appointment in the pilot. 95% or more of replies within 2 minutes. Nurse alerts within 30 seconds. At least 90% of routine bookings correct. Nurse-alert volume stays at a level the nurses accept.

gaps.question: Who receives and acknowledges nurse alerts at night and on weekends, and what happens if no one acknowledges one? The agent replies 24/7, but the nurse station app may not be staffed round the clock.
gaps.suggested: Name an on-call nurse for each pilot clinic outside opening hours. If an alert isn't acknowledged within 5 minutes, escalate to a second contact. Meanwhile the patient already has the 997 / ED advice. The agent never delays that advice while it waits for a nurse.
